I patch for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: drawer, edge swipes, readable settings, working right panel
# DSH Mobile UI
A phone-first fix for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI — a real drawer, edge swipes, readable settings an

d a working right panel, without touching the core.
DSH 0.2.x is desktop-first: a three-column grid,
a 188px settings nav, a 0px right panel and a 14px composer that makes iOS zoom the page. On a phon
e that leaves a sliver of chat, unreadable settings and no way to reach Files or the code viewer.

No more iOS auto-zoom — 16px fields on any touch device, even under a wide desktop layout
The chat k

eeps the width — a 56px rail plus an overlay drawer, with edge swipes
Everything else fits — setting
s, Files, terminal and the code viewer
No build step, no host code — one client module, MIT licensed.
## What it fixes
| Sidebar drawer | Settings | Files and code |
1. **iOS auto-zoom.** Safari zooms a focused field under 16px. All `input` / `textarea` / `contented
itable` become 16px on touch devices; the check is the *device* (`html.dsh-mf-touch`), not the viewp
ort width, so a phone showing a stretched desktop layout does not zoom either. `touch-action: manipu

lation` keeps double taps from moving the next tap off its target.
2. **The chat keeps the full widt
h.** The sidebar column stays a 56px rail; the open panel becomes a fixed overlay drawer with a dimm

ed, blurred scrim.
3. **The drawer closes** when you pick a session, when you tap outside it, and by

its own close button. The bottom safe area is respected.
4. **Session rows open on the first tap.**
iOS treats a plain `<div role="treeitem">` with a React handler as "not clickable" and holds its cl
ick for the double-tap window (~300ms). Closing the drawer first unmounted the row, so the tap only
closed the menu. The row's click is now dispatched synchronously from `pointerup`, and the late nati

ve click of the same tap is swallowed.
5. **Edge swipes.** Swipe from the left edge to open, swipe l
eft to close. Vertical drags stay with the scroller (36px threshold, 34px vertical drift, 24px edge

zone).
6. **Settings fit the phone.** The desktop dialog keeps a 188px nav column next to the conten
t — on a 390px screen that left ~150px. On narrow screens the section list becomes a horizontal, scr
ollable strip above the content, and the Account card stacks its identity above the "More account in

formation" link instead of squeezing the name into a narrow column.
7. **The right panel works.** DS
H already full-screens it below 768px; between 768 and 1023px the column kept a narrow track, so whi

le the panel is open (`data-sidebar-right-open`) the plugin promotes it to a full-screen sheet.
8. *
*Code and tables stay inside the message** and scroll on their own; code in the file viewer is 12px

instead of 11px.

## Before you install: make DSH reachable
`dsh --profile web` binds `127.0.0.1` by default — loopback only. A phone on the same Wi-Fi cannot o
pen it until you bind a real interface address and reopen the URL that carries the process token.
1. **Bind your machine's LAN address.** Wildcard addresses (`0.0.0.0`) are rejected by design; give
one concrete literal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. **Allow the port.** macOS asks once whether `node` may accept incoming connections — allow it. On
Windows add an inbound rule for that port, otherwise the phone times out silently.
3. **Open the printed URL on the phone.** Startup prints `dsh web: http://192.168.0.54:3080/?token=…
`. The token is per process: after a restart the old home-screen shortcut stops working, so re-add i
t (or paste the new link) — the current link is also in `~/.dsh/link.txt`.
4. **HTTPS is optional but changes what works.** Over plain HTTP on a LAN address the page is not a
secure context, so `navigator.share` is unavailable and the preview's bottom button reads **Download
file** instead of **Save to Files**; Chrome also refuses "Install app". iOS Safari still adds the p
age to the home screen over HTTP. For the full experience serve TLS:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Behind a prefix-stripping proxy or a tunnel, advertise the public root and trust its authority:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
5. **Only the Host machine shows "Open in <app>".** Those actions launch software on the machine run
ning DSH; the plugin hides them for remote clients. Force the answer with `localStorage['dsh-mobile-
fix-local'] = '1'` (local) or `'0'` (remote). `__dshMobileFixWhere()` in the page console prints the
decision, the address, the user agent and whether the page is a secure context.

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package is a plain DSH client plugin: `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one empty Host row, and `lib/cl
ient.js` is the browser bundle DSH serves through `dsh.client`. Everything it does is CSS and DOM ev
js` is the browser bundle DSH serves through `dsh.client`. Everything it does is CSS and DOM events:
- selectors use the stable halves of the CSS-module names (`sidebarCol`, `centerCol`, `rightbarCol`,

`sessionRow`, `_root`, `_collapsed`, `toggle`) and the public `data-slot` names;
- the phone layout

is behind `@media (max-width: 1023px)`, the 16px field rule is behind a touch-device class;
- one r
egistered listener set per page — a second `apply` (HMR, live composition) replaces the previous one
instead of stacking.
## Compatibility
| DSH | Profile | Checked on | Status |
| `0.2.1-rc.5` | `web` | Chromium fixture at 390×844 in CI, plus a real iPhone PWA by hand | tested

|
| other `0.2.x` | `web` | — | expected to work; a large layout redesign may need selector updates

|
| Android | `web` | Chromium with a Pixel 7 profile, Chrome 158 | layout works; see the Android no

te below |
| desktop ≥ 1024px | `web` | macOS Chrome / Safari | untouched by design |
## Limitations

- Selectors rely on CSS-module local names; a major redesign will need an update.
- The right panel

is presented as a sheet on phones, not resizable.
- No service worker, no Host code: this is a clien

t module only.
- Checked on iOS; Android Chrome should work (the layout rules are width-based) but i

.
- Checked on iOS; Android Chrome should work (the layout rules are width-based) but is not tested.
